prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in Conroe, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported whiplash. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1157; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The injury does not fit the crash: the impact was very light, yet the claimed injury is severe.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officer responded to a rear-end collision on a roadway in Conroe, Texas. Driver 1 was stopped in traffic when the vehicle operated by Driver 2 struck the rear of Driver 1's vehicle. Passenger was seated in the front passenger seat of Driver 1's vehicle, and both the responding officer and Driver 2 confirmed Passenger was present at the scene. Damage to the rear bumper of Driver 1's vehicle was visible but limited, and the impact appeared to be light. Driver 1 reported neck pain consistent with whiplash and described the injury as severe. The officer noted that the force of the impact seemed slight compared with the injury reported, and it is not clear whether all of the visible damage resulted from this collision. Scene photographs confirm vehicle positions and some of the damage, but no independent witnesses were located. No prior damage to Driver 1's vehicle was known to the officer or reported by either driver. Driver 1 is named on the insurance policy covering the vehicle.
